newsitem.title: USA: Freeze damage starts to show up in Oklahoma wheat.
newsitem.headline: Freeze damage starts to show up in Oklahoma wheat.

text.p: The condition of Oklahoma's wheat crop declined significantly in the week to Sunday due to freeze damage, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.

"Wheat conditions declined as freeze damage is beginning to show up. The damage varies from light to moderate in the Northeast and North Central districts to moderate to severe in the Panhandle and Southwestern districts," it said.

The winter wheat crop was rated four percent excellent, 38 percent good, 34 percent fair, eight percent poor and 16 percent very poor. A week earlier 66 percent of the crop had been in the good or excellent categories.
"It is still too early to tell the full extent of the damage. Diseases such as barley yellow dwarf, soil-borne mosaic virus and rust are being reported across the state," the report said.
Wheat was 97 percent jointing, up from 66 percent last year and a five-year average of 86 percent. It was 16 percent heading, versus five and 19 percent.
The freeze also damaged young corn plants across the state. "Many producers are gearing up to replant the damaged acres," the report said.
Corn was 19 percent planted, down from 22 percent a year ago and a five-year average of 32 percent.
